## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Monocular 3D pose per person
- Lightweight headless mesh model (e.g., SMPL-X-lite)
- On-device few-shot adaptation (LoRA-style adapters)
- Temporal consistency losses
- Privacy-preserving on-device inference

## Code Example
```python
class PoseInteractionModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, base, adapter_dim=8):
        super().__init__()
        self.base = base  # backbone
        self.adapter = LowRankAdapter(adapter_dim)
        self.classifier = InteractionHead()
    def forward(self, frames):
        feats = self.base(frames)
        feats = self.adapter(feats)
        pose3d = self.pose_head(feats)
        inter = self.classifier(feats, pose3d)
        return pose3d, inter
```

- What metrics and data pipelines would you use to validate privacy guarantees in production?

        super().__init__()
        self.backbone = ConvNeXtBackbone()

        self.seg_head = SegHead()

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses end-to-end design for real-world inventory sensing under occlusion, speed, and lighting variation, emphasizing self-supervised depth, differentiable 3D reasoning, and uncertainty estimation on edge hardware.

## Key Concepts
- Lightweight 2D detector (EfficientDet)
- Self-supervised depth from ego-motion
- Differentiable 3D box regression
- Uncertainty via MC dropout and aleatoric depth
- Kalman tracking + data association
- Edge deployment (latency, memory)

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode
function pipeline(frame, state){
  proposals = detector(frame)
  depth = depthFromMotion(frame, state)
  boxes = reg3D(proposals, depth)
  tracks = kalmanTrack(boxes, state)
  return tracks
}
```

- How would you evaluate robustness to motion blur and occlusion?
- How would you adapt the system to different pallet shapes/sizes or new warehouses without labeled data?
